h: Scores, Strategy and a Spot of City Sightseeing
p: Bowling scoring confuses more people than it should, so here's the cheat sheet. Each game is ten frames. Knock everything down with your first ball and that's a strike, worth ten plus whatever your next two balls score. Clear the rest with your second ball and that's a spare, worth ten plus your next ball. A perfect game is 300, which is twelve strikes in a row. Don't worry, the screens do the maths; you just need to know when to celebrate.

Before your game, take a walk around one of Birmingham's best-known spots. The bronze bull statue by the Bullring is the go-to photo stop, and St Martin's Church sits right below the shopping centre, a lovely old church surrounded by modern glass. The Selfridges building with its shiny discs is a sight in its own right. The historic Bull Ring markets nearby are worth a browse too.

If you've got time to spare, Digbeth is a short walk away and is known for its street art, independent bars and food. New Street station is close by for anyone coming in by train, which makes it a doddle for groups meeting from different directions.
Booking tip: weekend evenings fill up fast in the city centre, so get a slot reserved and arrive ten minutes early to sort shoes and drinks before you start.
